queries: WITH per_type AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM per_type), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.tradekind, s.cnt AS behaviour_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC

responses.sql: WITH per_type AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM per_type), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.tradekind, s.cnt AS behaviour_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC

assumptions.assumption: "How much behaviour analysis" means the number of advancedbehavior rows per trader type, counted after inner joins advancedbehavior -> transactionrecord -> trader. Rows that fail to match are dropped.
A NULL tradekind forms its own group. GROUP BY puts NULLs together, so no extra handling is needed.
The average share is the plain average of the per-type shares, with each type counted once. If there are no groups the average is NULL and no rows are returned.

responses.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord r ON a.translink = r.transreg JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM g), x AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT tradekind, cnt AS analysis_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM x WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: The amount of behaviour analysis for a trader type is the number of advancedbehavior rows that reach a trader through the inner joins (translink = transreg, then trdref = tradereg). Rows with no match are dropped.
A NULL tradekind forms its own group, because GROUP BY keeps NULLs together. The average is taken over all groups, including that one.
If there are no groups, or the average is NULL, the final comparison returns no rows.

responses.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord r ON a.translink = r.transreg JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt::numeric / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), g AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT tradekind, cnt AS behaviour_analysis_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM g WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Each advancedbehavior row counts as one behaviour analysis. Inner joins through transactionrecord to trader drop unmatched rows. A NULL tradekind forms its own group.
The average is the plain mean of the per-type shares, with each type weighted equally. The comparison is strict, so if the average is NULL no rows are returned.
